title: Stilling the mind
hookLine: yoga is the stilling of the mind's movements (Yoga Sutras 1.2)
last: YOGA BEGINS WITH HOW YOU TREAT PEOPLE.

lines: LINE ONE: NOW, THE TEACHING OF YOGA.
cards: The Yoga Sutras don't warm up. The first line is barely a sentence: now, the teaching of yoga. The second line is the definition, and the whole book hangs on it.
No poses. No breath. No gods, yet.
Just a claim about what's going on behind your eyes, all day: the mind is moving. It flickers from a memory to a worry to a plan, to a song from a commercial, to the memory again.
Yoga, the second line says, is what happens when that stills.

teach.h: THE STILLING OF THE MIND'S MOVEMENTS.
teach.b: Sutra one point two: yogash chitta vritti nirodhah. Yoga is the stilling of the movements of the mind. Translators reach for different English.
Chitta is the mind, or the whole field of awareness. Vritti has been put as movements, fluctuations, modifications, whirls; nirodha as restraint, cessation, stilling.

teach.h: THE SEER RESTS IN ITS OWN NATURE.
teach.b: Then the next line: when that happens, the seer rests in its own nature. Otherwise, the line after says, the seer takes on the shape of the movements: angry when the anger moves, anxious when the worry moves.
The book lists the kinds of movement, and there are five: right knowledge, error, imagination, sleep and memory. Right knowledge is on the list. So is sleep.
The stilling isn't only about clearing out bad thoughts. Even true thoughts are movements. So how does it happen?
Sutra one point twelve answers in two words: practice, and non-attachment. Practice is coming back. Non-attachment is letting go of what pulls you away.
And practice becomes firm, the book adds, when it's kept up for a long time, without a break, and with care. One image teachers reach for is a lake.
When the wind drops, the surface goes flat, and you can see straight down to the bottom.
The water was always clear. It was just moving.

how: Students of the Yoga Sutras learn sutra 1.2 as the definition of yoga and practice stilling the mind in seated meditation, coming back again and again, with non-attachment to whatever pulls them away.

o: emptying the mind of every bad thought by force
slowing the breath until the heartbeat drops
Patanjali's yoga: the mind's movements growing still

games.q: stilling the mind: tap the pairs.
p: the mind, the field of awareness

s: the stilling in sutra 1.2 is only about clearing out bad thoughts
the book's list of movements includes right knowledge, and even sleep.
when the mind isn't still, the seer takes the shape of its movements
that's the line right after the definition: otherwise, the seer looks like whatever is moving.
the sutras say the stilling comes quickly, with the right technique
practice becomes firm when kept up for a long time, without a break, and with care.

games.q: you sit down and your mind is racing. by sutra 1.12, what stills it?
games.why: practice, the coming back, and non-attachment, letting go of what pulls you away. two words carry the whole method.

practice: Choose a position you can hold without fidgeting, decide not to move until the bell, and let the body be the first thing that stills. Then watch the mind move, a memory, a plan, a sound, without chasing or fighting any of it.
Each time you notice you've been carried off, that's the practice: come back to sitting still.

wordCard.voice: Stilling the mind. Patanjali's definition of yoga: the movements of the mind grow still, and the seer rests in its own nature. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit, from Yoga Sutras 1.2: the stilling of the movements of the mind.
